claims.text: sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) triggers a checkpoint after a commit when the WAL contains at least N frames.
claims.quote: automatically checkpoint after committing a transaction if there are N or more frames in the write-ahead log file.

claims.text: Passing N less than or equal to zero to sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint disables automatic checkpoints entirely.
claims.quote: Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.

claims.text: Each new database connection enables automatic checkpointing with a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.
claims.quote: Every new database connection defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.

claims.text: Continuously overlapping readers can prevent checkpoints from completing and allow unbounded WAL growth.
claims.quote: if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.

claims.text: Attempting checkpoints during intervals with no readers can avoid checkpoint starvation.
claims.quote: This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are "reader gaps": times when no processes are reading from the database and that checkpoints are attempted during those times.

claims.text: The WAL must reach persistent storage before checkpointing moves its content into the database.
claims.quote: The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database

claims.text: PRAGMA synchronous=FULL syncs the WAL at every transaction commit, whereas NORMAL omits that commit sync.
claims.quote: Writers sync the WAL on every transaction commit if PRAGMA synchronous is set to FULL but omit this sync if PRAGMA synchronous is set to NORMAL.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE checkpoints available frames without waiting for readers or writers to finish.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE never invokes the busy-handler callback.
claims.quote: The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode. On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL waits until no writer exists and all readers use the most recent database snapshot.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback ) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot.

claims.text: While SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL is pending, it blocks new writers but permits new readers.
claims.quote: This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.

claims.text: After checkpointing, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART additionally waits until all readers read only from the database file.
claims.quote: after checkpointing the log file it blocks (calls the busy-handler callback ) until all readers are reading from the database file only.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART ensures that the next writer restarts the WAL from its beginning.
claims.quote: This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE adds zero-byte WAL truncation immediately before a successful return to RESTART behavior.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP checkpoints zero frames and exposes checkpoint status through pnLog and pnCkpt.
claims.quote: This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.

claims.text: pnCkpt includes frames checkpointed before the current function call.
claims.quote: the total number of checkpointed frames in the log file (including any that were already checkpointed before the function was called)

claims.text: Failure to obtain the checkpoint lock because another process is checkpointing returns SQLITE_BUSY.
claims.quote: If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned.

claims.text: A checkpoint-lock conflict does not invoke a configured busy handler.
claims.quote: Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.

claims.text: If the busy handler returns zero while waiting for the writer lock or readers, checkpointing falls back to PASSIVE behavior and returns SQLITE_BUSY.
claims.quote: the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE - checkpointing as many frames as possible without blocking any further. SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case.

claims.text: Ordinary checkpointing normally reuses the WAL from its beginning rather than truncating it, unless journal_size_limit is set.
claims.quote: The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning.

claims.text: The last connection to close performs a final checkpoint and deletes the WAL and associated shared-memory file.
claims.quote: When the last connection to a database closes, that connection does one last checkpoint and then deletes the WAL and its associated shared-memory file, to clean up the disk.

claims.text: By default, the thread whose COMMIT pushes the WAL over its size limit runs the automatic checkpoint.
claims.quote: By default, the checkpoint will be run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit.

claims.text: Applications can disable automatic checkpointing and schedule periodic checkpoints in a separate thread or process.
claims.quote: the application can disable automatic checkpointing and run the periodic checkpoints in a separate thread, or separate process.

claims.text: Infrequent checkpoints amortize checkpoint cost across more writes by allowing a larger WAL.
claims.quote: To maximize write performance, one wants to amortize the cost of each checkpoint over as many writes as possible, meaning that one wants to run checkpoints infrequently

claims.text: A concurrent checkpoint must stop before passing any current reader's end mark.
claims.quote: A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader.

claims.text: The shared-memory wal-index helps readers locate WAL pages quickly with minimal I/O.
claims.quote: a data structure called the "wal-index" is maintained in shared memory which helps readers locate pages in the WAL quickly and with a minimum of I/O.

claims.text: The wal-index shared-memory requirement confines readers to one machine and prevents this WAL implementation from working on a network filesystem.
claims.quote: the use of shared memory means that all readers must exist on the same machine. This is why the write-ahead log implementation will not work on a network filesystem.

claims.text: Registering sqlite3_wal_hook disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint.
claims.quote: Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by this function.

claims.text: A NULL or empty zDb dispatches the checkpoint operation to all attached WAL databases and leaves pnLog and pnCkpt undefined.
claims.quote: If parameter zDb is NULL or points to a zero length string, then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db. In this case the values written to output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt are undefined.

claims.text: When an attached database returns SQLITE_BUSY, processing continues for remaining attached databases and ultimately returns SQLITE_BUSY.
claims.quote: If an SQLITE_BUSY error is encountered when processing one or more of the attached WAL databases, the operation is still attempted on any remaining attached databases and SQLITE_BUSY is returned at the end.

claims.text: The WAL cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.
claims.quote: A checkpoint can only complete when no other transactions are running, which means the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.

claims.text: WAL readers and writers can run concurrently, but only one writer can operate at a time.
claims.quote: writers and readers can run at the same time. However, since there is only one WAL file, there can only be one writer at a time.

claims.text: Rollback journaling saves original database content separately before writing changes directly into the database.
claims.quote: The traditional rollback journal works by writing a copy of the original unchanged database content into a separate rollback journal file and then writing changes directly into the database file.

claims.text: The database file must be synced before the WAL is reset.
claims.quote: and the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL.

claims.text: Read performance deteriorates as WAL size increases, even with the wal-index.
claims.quote: The wal-index helps find content in the WAL file much faster, but performance still falls off with increasing WAL file size.
